title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide
author: Avery Chen
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s standard practices for hiring, candidate evaluation, employee onboarding, first-90-days plans, performance and feedback cycles, and manager responsibilities. It is intended as the canonical reference for hiring managers, interviewers, people-ops, and new managers. Where templates and links are referenced, use the related pages listed above or contact people-ops@redwood.com.

Scope

Applies to: all full-time and contractor hires, internal transfers, managers involved in interviewing/hiring, and people-ops staff who support the process. Does not replace role-specific competency frameworks maintained in team-level docs; instead, it defines the company-level process and manager obligations.

1) Hiring process: end-to-end flow

Short intro: Our hiring flow is designed to be candidate-friendly, consistent, and calibrated for fairness and performance. Timelines below are targets; exceptions require approval from the recruiting lead.

Phases (table):
| Phase | Owner | Target timeline | Deliverables |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Requisition & role definition | Hiring manager + People Ops | 1-3 days | Requisition, JD, scorecard |
| Sourcing & screening | Recruiting | 1-3 weeks | Candidate slate, initial screen notes |
| Interview loop | Hiring manager + panel | 1-2 weeks | Interview feedback, consensus decision |
| Offer & negotiation | Hiring manager + People Ops | 3-7 days | Signed offer, background check initiated |
| Onboarding & first 90 days | Manager + People Ops | 90 days | Onboarding checklist complete, ramp plan |

Step-by-step:
1. Requisition: hiring manager completes the role requisition form (HRIS link) and attaches the role scorecard. People-ops will verify budget and submit to recruiting.
2. Scorecard definition: before any interviews are scheduled, the hiring manager completes a scorecard that defines three core competencies for the role (must be observable and job-related), expected impact in the first 6 months, and non-negotiables.
3. Sourcing: recruiting sources candidates from internal referrals, LinkedIn, targeted outreach, and diversity pipelines. Initial phone screen (30 minutes) verifies interest, basic fit, and core competencies.
4. Interview loop: four to five interviews maximum for IC roles; up to six for senior hires (including a bar-raiser or cross-functional partner). Interviewers use the scorecard and submit structured feedback within 24 hours of interview completion.
5. Decision & calibration: hiring manager collates feedback and runs a short calibration call with people-ops and a peer manager if feedback is mixed. Final decision documented in the applicant tracking system (ATS).
6. Offer: people-ops drafts offer letter with compensation, equity, and start date. Compensation exceptions (above band or special equity grants) require VP approval.

Interviewing guidance and expectations

- Interviewers must complete the panel calibration training (annual).
- Use behavioral and work-sample questions tied to the scorecard; avoid hypothetical or brainteaser questions.
- Give candidates time to ask questions and summarize next steps at the end of each interview.
- Submit structured feedback using the ATS template with numeric ratings and written evidence for each competency.
- Disqualifiers: safety risk, dishonest background, or inability to perform critical must-have competencies after reasonable accommodation.

Scorecard template (example)

Role: Senior ML Engineer
Top competencies:
- System design for inference pipelines (observable: design exercises, past project evidence)
- Ownership & execution (observable: project write-ups, timelines)
- Collaboration and cross-functional communication (observable: examples of stakeholder management)

Must-haves: experience designing production-grade inference systems; familiarity with GPU runtimes or distributed inference preferred.

2) Offer and background checks

- Standard lead time between verbal offer and written offer: 48 hours.
- Background checks: initiated at offer acceptance; adverse findings escalate to people-ops.
- Start date changes: if a candidate requests > 60 days delay, manager must notify people-ops and confirm headcount/backfill impact.

3) Onboarding: first 90 days (manager + people-ops responsibilities)

Intro paragraph: A successful ramp combines clear expectations, early wins, and structured support. The manager owns the role-specific ramp; people-ops owns cross-company onboarding and benefits setup.

Onboarding checklist (first week):
- Pre-start: equipment and accounts ordered (IT), benefits enrollment sent (people-ops), welcome note & calendar invites created (manager).
- Day 1: orientation session with People Ops (90 minutes), HR paperwork complete, badge/access provided, team welcome lunch.
- Week 1: role overview, core system walkthroughs, meet 1:1 with direct stakeholders, set 30/60/90 goals.

First 30/60/90 expectations (numbered):
1. 30 days: understand product and team priorities, complete training modules (security, codebase, infra), deliver a small, scoped contribution or bug fix.
2. 60 days: own a medium-sized ticket or feature end-to-end with coaching; demonstrate cross-team interactions.
3. 90 days: independently own a recurring part of the service, present a ramp progress review with manager and people-ops, and have measurable customer impact.

Manager checklist (onboarding):
- Provide written 30/60/90 plan within 48 hours of start.
- Schedule weekly 1:1s in calendar for first 90 days.
- Assign a peer buddy and an onboarding project.
- Confirm training completion and access to required systems.

4) Performance and feedback cycle

Overview: Redwood uses a continuous feedback culture complemented by two formal review cycles per year: mid-year (June) and year-end (December). Managers are accountable for ensuring ongoing coaching, tracking objectives, and documenting performance evidence.

Core elements:
- Objectives: teams adopt quarterly objectives that tie to product or operational goals. Objectives are not strictly OKRs but should be measurable and aligned with company priorities.
- Ongoing feedback: provide timely feedback within 72 hours of key events (launches, incidents, demos). Use private written feedback in the HRIS for record-keeping where appropriate.
- Formal reviews: manager writes a draft narrative, team peer feedback is collected, calibration is run by people-ops and leadership, and final ratings are communicated with a calibration note.

Review timeline (high level):
- 6 weeks prior: managers start collecting evidence and soliciting peer feedback.
- 2 weeks prior: draft review submitted to people-ops.
- Calibration week: people-ops hosts calibration panels by level and function.
- Final: manager delivers review and sets development plan.

Performance rating guide (short):
- Exceeds expectations: consistently delivers above role expectations; measurable impact and leadership.
- Meets expectations: reliably delivers the role’s core responsibilities.
- Needs improvement: not meeting core responsibilities; manager must create a performance improvement plan (PIP) or development plan.

Feedback and coaching best practices

- Use the SBI model (Situation, Behavior, Impact) for constructive feedback.
- Balance growth-oriented feedback with recognition of contributions.
- Document recurring patterns of concern and escalate to people-ops for coordinated support.
- If performance concerns persist after documented coaching (60-90 days), manager and people-ops will assess next steps (additional coaching, role change, or PIP).

5) Manager-specific guidance and responsibilities

Manager expectations summary: hire and retain great talent, create clarity on priorities, provide regular feedback, and run reliable one-on-ones and calibration.

Checklist for managers:
- Before hiring: write a clear scorecard, align on compensation band with people-ops, and identify interviewers.
- During hiring: participate in panel interviews, complete structured feedback, and drive the decision timeline.
- Onboarding: provide the 30/60/90 plan and assign a buddy.

- Career conversations: at least one formal career conversation per year and quarterly informal check-ins.
- Performance management: prepare evidence, run reviews on schedule, and attend calibration panels.

Manager templates (examples to copy from people-ops):
- 30/60/90 plan template (copyable):
  * 30-day goals:
    - Learn core systems and team workflows
    - Complete onboarding trainings: Security 101, Code of Conduct, Infra Access
    - Deliver small scoped contribution
  * 60-day goals:
    - Lead a medium feature or incident response
    - Improve an internal process or doc
  * 90-day goals:
    - Demonstrate independent ownership of a component
    - Present ramp progress to stakeholders

- Sample prompts for career conversations:
  1) What would you like to do more of at Redwood?
  2) Which skills do you want to build over the next 6-12 months?
  3) What role-level stretch assignments interest you?

6) Transitions, role changes, and offboarding

- Internal transfers: treat like a new hire for ramp planning but skip background checks. Hiring manager must coordinate with the current manager to align timelines and knowledge transfer.
- Promotions: manager prepares a promotion packet with impact summary and calibration notes. People-ops maintains promotion bands and approvals.
- Offboarding: manager initiates offboarding in HRIS, schedule knowledge transfer, revoke access on last day unless an exit extension is approved by security. Exit interviews are conducted within 5 business days.

7) Templates and sample artifacts

- Offer email subject line and short template (example):
  Subject: Redwood Inference — Offer for [Role]
  Hi [Candidate],

  We’re excited to offer you the position of [Role] on our [Team]. Attached is the formal offer letter with compensation and start date. Please let us know any questions and confirm by replying to this email by [Date].

  Best,
  [Hiring Manager] and People Ops

- Sample interview feedback entry (ATS):
  "Competency: System Design — Rating: 4/5 — Evidence: Designed a sharded KV cache for low-latency retrieval; explained tradeoffs on consistency vs. latency; delivered a production rollout plan."

8) Compliance, security & privacy considerations

- New hires are required to complete Security 101 and Data Handling training in the first 14 days.
- Managers must ensure contractors signed appropriate NDA and SAs prior to granting access to customer data.
- Background checks and right-to-work documentation must be stored in the secure HR system and handled per retention policy.

9) FAQs and common scenarios

Q: What if a candidate needs more than 60 days to start?
A: Approve only when business needs allow; the hiring manager must confirm headcount and coordinate with people-ops to revalidate the offer and salary band.

Q: How do I escalate a hiring freeze or headcount question?
A: Contact finance-ops and your leadership sponsor; people-ops will broker the discussion.

Q: What resources are available for first-time managers?
A: People-ops runs an eight-week manager onboarding program (recordings and materials are in the learning portal).

10) Related resources and ownership

Owners: People Ops (process, offer templates, compliance), Recruiting (sourcing & initial screen), Hiring Managers (scorecard, interviews, onboarding), People Managers (ongoing performance), Security (access & offboarding).

Links: See related pages at the top of this doc for templates, scorecards, and manager training materials.
